title: Change the Key of a Practice Track on iPhone
description: Move a local backing track into a better singing range on iPhone. Count the semitones, keep the original tempo and check your new key.
direct: Count the semitones between the old and target keys, lower the pitch, then verify the song against a reference.
figureAlt: Rehearsal room with a guitarist and singer using a keyboard to check a reference note
cards.decision.heading: Find a key that fits
cards.decision.body: To shift G major down to F major, count two semitones: G to F-sharp to F. The old G–C–D chords become F–B-flat–C. Sing the high phrase first, then the lowest phrase to check the whole range.
sections.detail-1.heading: Check the whole phrase
sections.detail-1.body: Listen for the point where the key change feels most useful. A lead note can guide a quick pitch check, but the surrounding chords tell you whether the backing track fits the whole arrangement. Keep a normal-pitch copy for playing with the original recording.
sections.detail-2.heading: About the app
sections.detail-2.body: Space Sheep Studio develops this iPhone app. Check the App Store listing for current access and export options.
faqs.first-question.heading: Can I import a streaming download?
faqs.first-question.body: Use a local audio file that other apps can open. Streaming apps may restrict access to their downloads.
faqs.second-question.heading: Will voices sound identical?
faqs.second-question.body: Pitch changes can affect the character of vocals and instruments. Listen to a short section before exporting the whole track.

steps.step-1.text: Open a local copy in Audio Compressor MP3 Converter.
steps.step-2.text: Lower the pitch by two semitones if the control shows semitones. Leave tempo at its starting value.
steps.step-3.text: Check the first chord against a keyboard, then export and name your practice copy with the new key.
